elements.element: Renewal occurs either only by mutual written agreement or through automatic twelve-month renewal terms.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 provides for automatic twelve-month renewals, satisfying the automatic-renewal alternative.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out by giving no more than thirty days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires sixty days' advance written notice, rather than allowing Customer to opt out on thirty days' notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must provide Customer a renewal reminder sixty days before renewal.
elements.evidence: The operative clause contains no Vendor renewal-reminder obligation. The margin comment is non-operative.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and three percent.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 expressly caps increases at the lesser of the preceding twelve-month CPI increase and three percent.

elements.element: Renewal is automatic unless timely non-renewal notice is given.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 states that each Order Form renews unless either Party gives advance written notice.

elements.element: The non-renewal notice window is no more than sixty days.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires exactly sixty days' advance written notice.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase is no more than five percent.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 imposes the stricter cap of the lesser of CPI and three percent, which is no more than five percent.

result.reason: The redline minimally changes the non-renewal window from 180 to 60 days and therefore fully reaches the fallback. It does not reach the preferred position because Customer is not permitted to opt out on 30 days' notice and Vendor has no operative duty to provide a 60-day renewal reminder. The existing CPI/3% cap satisfies both price-increase standards.
